keyVerseText: Of Heman: the sons of Heman; Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, and Romamtiezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth: Uzziel: also called, Azareel, ver.18. Shebuel: also called, Shubael, ver.20.
rootMeaning: The root of אֱלִיאָתָה (ʼĔlîyʼâthâh) is derived from אֵל (ʼêl), meaning God or mighty one, combined with אוּת, suggesting a sense of divine agreement or presence. The etymology conveys the meaning 'God of (his) consent' or more simply 'God has come.' This literal sense enriches the common English gloss by emphasizing not only the name but the theological affirmation that God is present and actively involved.
usageInScripture: The word אֱלִיאָתָה occurs twice in Scripture, consistently rendered as 'Eliathah' or 'to Eliathah.' It is used as a proper name, specifically identifying an Israelite individual, a Hemanite musician in David's court. This consistent usage as a personal name highlights its role in identifying a person whose name carries significant theological meaning rather than serving as a common noun or title.
theologicalSignificance: The name אֱלִיאָתָה, meaning 'God has come,' carries profound theological weight, reminding believers of God's active presence and intervention in human history. It reflects the reality that God is not distant but has come near, a truth foundational to Christian faith in the incarnation of Christ. The presence of such a name in the worship context of David's court underscores the centrality of God's nearness in worship and service. It encourages believers to trust in God's powerful and present help in all circumstances.
keyVerseReflection: 1 Chronicles 25:4 lists Eliathah among the sons of Heman, who served as musicians in David's court. The inclusion of Eliathah here, whose name means 'God has come,' enriches the passage by reminding readers that those who lead in worship are themselves marked by the reality of God's presence. This suggests that worship is not merely ritual but an encounter with the living God who has come to dwell among His people.
